Fictional chipmaker Nimbus Silicon delays its N3 accelerator to 2027

Nimbus Silicon, a fictional chip company used in this test, said on Tuesday that it will delay the launch of its N3 AI accelerator from late 2026 to the second quarter of 2027. The company told investors that a packaging supplier needed more time to qualify a new high-bandwidth memory stack, and that early samples did not meet its power target of 450 watts.

The delay changes the company's product plan. Nimbus will keep shipping its current N2 accelerator through 2027 and will offer existing customers a software update that it says improves N2 inference throughput by up to 18 percent. The company also lowered its full-year revenue guidance to 2.1 billion dollars from 2.4 billion dollars.

According to the company, the delay matters because several cloud providers had planned to build new clusters around N3. Nimbus said it is talking with those customers about interim capacity based on N2 systems, but it did not name any of them.

The company cautioned that the new date depends on the supplier passing qualification in January, and said it could not rule out a further delay. It also said the 18 percent figure was measured on its own internal benchmark and may differ for other workloads.
